scenarios.title: Each text operator follows its definition and is case-sensitive
scenarios.notes: Risk: a wrong operator or a case fold launches names a rule rejects. Try starts_with, ends_with and contains with matching and non-matching samples. Try case pairs (Feature/ vs feature/x, -E2E vs e2e, Feature in feature/x). Try an empty pattern, an empty sample, a pattern equal to the sample, and unicode case (the dotless i, the German sharp s). Call through the module entry point with python3 -I.

scenarios.title: A regex rule uses search and an uncompilable pattern gives None
scenarios.notes: Risk: match instead of search, or a raised re.error. Check ^sdlc/ and S-001 and ^S-001 on sdlc/S-001. Check the patterns ( and [a- and a lone backslash give None. Security angle: patterns that raise RecursionError or OverflowError, nested quantifiers on a long sample (hang), a NUL in the pattern or sample, and a huge repeat count. The spec says evaluate catches only re.error, so record any other exception as an observation, not a silent pass.

scenarios.title: Negate flips True and False and keeps None
scenarios.notes: Risk: negate turns None into True. Check negate on all four kinds for a match and a non-match. Check negate on an uncompilable regex gives None. Check negate values that are not booleans (0, 1, absent, null) follow plain truthiness and never raise.

scenarios.title: An unknown or malformed rule never raises and gives None
scenarios.notes: Risk: a GitHub operator outside the four kinds crashes the pre-flight (ADR-6e23). Try kind equals, empty kind, absent kind, null kind, kind in a different case (Starts_With), with negate true and false. Security angle: a pattern or sample of a non-string type (None, number, list). Record whether it raises, because the slice promises None only for an unknown kind. Confirm evaluate writes nothing to disk and prints nothing.

scenarios.title: regex_error reports the compile error text or None
scenarios.notes: Risk: S-012 needs the text for its note (ADR-b582). Check regex_error of ( and [a- returns a non-empty string. Check ^a and the empty pattern return None. Check the text equals the str of the re.error that evaluate hides.

tools.purpose: Seeded generator and batch caller for evaluate and regex_error through pycall.py
Hostile pattern and sample strings for evaluate

riskReason: evaluate feeds the pre-flight verdict, so a wrong True launches names a rule rejects, but it is a pure function with one boundary.
notes: Limits is not tagged: the spec states no number for evaluate. A pattern that backtracks without end is a concern for the security profile, as plan.md says it adds no timeout.
